judgments.reason: The data confirms that coal still provided 3.4% of electricity in 2025, meaning complete phase-out has not been achieved.
With gas accounting for 79.7% of total generation in 2025, any disruption to supply would indeed impact the majority of the power system.

requirements.evidence: Renewables rose by 15% between 2015 and 2025, reaching 16.9% of Israel's electricity.
requirements.reason: The report gives the 2025 share and the absolute percentage point change, but misstates the relative growth rate as 15% instead of the actual absolute increase of 15 percentage points.

requirements.evidence: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity, so the phase-out is far from complete.
requirements.reason: The report states Israel's coal status in 2025, though it cites an incorrect percentage value (14.3% instead of 3.4%).
The report fails to include any comparison with Mediterranean peers.

requirements.evidence: Total generation increased from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh over the decade.
requirements.reason: The report accurately provides Israel's total electricity generation growth between 2015 and 2025.

requirements.evidence: Israel's reliance on gas (79.7% of generation in 2025) is the main vulnerability: any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system.
requirements.reason: The report identifies heavy reliance on gas as a key risk and grounds it directly in the 2025 data.
